newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Talks resume to resolve Colombia port strike.
newsitem.headline: Talks resume to resolve Colombia port strike.

text.p: Union boss Nelson Amaya said he hoped for a rapid breakthrough in talks to end the eight-day-old dockworkers' strike at Colombia's main Pacific coast port as negotiations restarted at midday local/1700 GMT Wednesday.

Dockers' representatives, cargo handling operators and ship owners suspended initial talks in the early hours Wednesday after they failed to reach agreement on a four-point framework agreement in an 11-hour meeting.

The strike at the port of Buenaventura has blocked exports of more than 300,000 60-kg bags of coffee and 27,000 tonnes of sugar. The port is estimated to be losing $500,000 for every day of the strike.

"We're all around the table again and I'm hopeful we can reach a rapid solution today after last nights talks," said Amaya, regional head of the Unitary Workers'Confederation (CUT), to which the main dock workers' union is affiliated.

The four-point basic agreement, if approved, will almost double dockers' wages, from the current average of less than $80 per month, and grant sickness, injury and social security benefits as well as meal allowances.
It would also provide for the creation of committees to look at more complex aspects of worker demands, such as the way the port operates and the way they are contracted.
